newsitem.title: USA: Renaissance Cruises sues debtors in London, NY.
newsitem.headline: Renaissance Cruises sues debtors in London, NY.

text.p: Renaissance Cruises Inc said on Monday it had filed lawsuits in New York and London against bank debtors it claims are not honoring loan-restructuring pacts hammered out in 1994 and 1996.

"The binding written commitments made to us have been ignored, and our efforts to have the banks honor their promises have been to no avail," Renaissance chairman Edward Rudner said in a brief news release.
Credit Lyonnais of France and Christiana Bank of Norway were among the banks named in the lawsuits, the company said.

The company said the London suit relates to a contractual dispute and the New York one claims wrongful detention of funds. A Renaissance spokesman said the U.S. suit was filed in State Supreme Court for New York but said he could provide no further details on the disputes.

Owner of eight cruise ships, Renaissance signed in late 1994 a debt-restructuring agreement with Intituto Bancario San Paolo and Christiana. A second deal was reached in August 1996, which required the sale of some Renaissance vessels with an eye to cutting the cruise company's debts.

Renaissance identified the banks being sued as: Banca Caige SpA, Christiana Bank og Kreditkasse, Credit Lyonnais, Fokus Bahk, Instituto Bancario San Paulo di Torino SpA, Skadinviska Enskilda Banken and Sparenbank NOR.
Privately held Renaissance last fall ordered construction of two non-smoking cruise ships at an estimated cost of $300 million.
